blocks.text: If the compiler knows the fix for an error it writes it next to the error and **verifies** it by trying it on a copy (`fix (verified)`). `gg fix` applies the verified fixes to the file and repeats until none are left.

code: gg fix                 # every .gg file in the folder
gg fix --dry-run       # only print what would be done
gg fix --likely        # also apply guess-based fixes that compile

blocks.text: There are two kinds of fix: **`safe`** (the one sensible repair: spellings from other languages such as `&&`, `||`, `x++`, `;`, `let x = 5`, a forgotten `:` at the end of a line, a missing `import std.math`...) and **`likely`** (a guess that compiles: a misspelled name, a missing `match` arm, an `i32(...)` conversion...).
`gg fmt` brings every file to a single layout: four spaces per block, `else`/`elif` aligned with their `if`, no trailing whitespace. Running it a second time changes nothing.

code: gg fmt --check src/     # only check (for CI)

options: Only prints what would be done

blocks.q: Which command only checks formatting in CI?
blocks.why: `--check` does not change files; it exits with an error code if they differ.
